records.source: Τότε ὁμοιωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν δέκα παρθένοις, αἵτινες λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου.
records.gloss: Then will be likened the kingdom of the heavens to ten virgins, who having taken the lamps of them went forth to meeting of the bridegroom.
pieces: At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young women who were bridesmaids. They took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

L.1: Then the kingdom of the heavens will be like ten virgins, who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

R.1: When that day comes, the kingdom of heaven will be like this. Ten young women were bridesmaids at a wedding. They took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

decisions.choice: then: when the Son of Man comes, as in 24:44-51
decisions.reason: The parable continues the teaching about the Son of Man's coming that began at 24:4. "Then" points to that day.

decisions.choice: virgins: unmarried young women, here serving as bridesmaids
alternatives: a statement about their moral life
decisions.reason: The word names young women of marrying age who were not yet married. The story is about their part in the wedding, not their purity.

decisions.choice: going out to meet the bridegroom: a wedding custom
alternatives: meeting him at the bride's home only
decisions.reason: A bridegroom went to fetch his bride and brought her to his home, often in the evening. Friends of the couple met the procession with lamps and went in with them to the feast.

decisions.choice: to meet the bridegroom, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: to meet the bridegroom and the bride, the reading of some manuscripts and early translations
decisions.reason: Some Greek and Latin and Syriac witnesses add "and the bride". Most manuscripts end with the bridegroom alone, and the story speaks only of him. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: young women who were bridesmaids
decisions.reason: "Virgins" draws attention to something the story is not about. Balanced and Readable say who they were and what they were doing; Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: When that day comes
decisions.reason: Readable says what "then" refers to, following the meaning decision.

records.heading: Ten bridesmaids wait for the bridegroom

records.source: πέντε δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἦσαν μωραὶ καὶ πέντε φρόνιμοι.
records.gloss: Five now of them were foolish and five wise.
pieces: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

L.2: Now five of them were foolish, and five [were] wise.

R.2: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

decisions.choice: foolish, wise: lacking or showing good sense about what is coming
decisions.reason: The same pair describes the two builders in 7:24-27. Wisdom here is being ready; folly is not thinking ahead.

records.source: αἱ γὰρ μωραὶ λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔλαβον μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν ἔλαιον·
records.gloss: The for foolish having taken the lamps of them not did take with themselves oil;
pieces: The foolish ones took their lamps but brought no oil along with them.

L.3: For the foolish, taking their lamps, did not take oil with them;

R.3: The foolish bridesmaids took their lamps, but they did not take any extra oil with them.

decisions.choice: lamps: torches or small oil lamps carried at night
decisions.reason: The word can mean a torch, a pole wrapped with rags soaked in oil, or a lamp. Either way it needed a fresh supply of oil to keep burning. The story does not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: no oil with them: no supply beyond what was in the lamps
decisions.reason: Their lamps were burning but going out by 25:8, so the lack is a spare supply.

decisions.choice: extra oil
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the lamps had some oil, following the meaning decision.

records.source: αἱ δὲ φρόνιμοι ἔλαβον ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μετὰ τῶν λαμπάδων ἑαυτῶν.
records.gloss: The but wise took oil in the vessels with the lamps of them.
pieces: But the wise ones took flasks of oil as well as their lamps.

L.4: But the wise took oil in flasks along with their lamps.

R.4: But the wise ones took jars of oil with them, as well as their lamps.

decisions.choice: vessels: small containers for carrying oil
decisions.reason: The word is a general one for a container. It is separate from the lamps.

records.source: χρονίζοντος δὲ τοῦ νυμφίου ἐνύσταξαν πᾶσαι καὶ ἐκάθευδον.
records.gloss: Tarrying then the bridegroom they became drowsy all and were sleeping.
pieces: When the bridegroom was late in coming, every one of them nodded off and slept.

L.5: And while the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and were sleeping.

R.5: The bridegroom was late. All the young women got sleepy and fell asleep.

decisions.choice: tarrying: delayed, slow to come
decisions.reason: The same verb describes the slave's thought "my master is delayed" in 24:48. The delay is part of the lesson about watching.

decisions.choice: all slept: the wise as well as the foolish
decisions.reason: Sleep is not the fault. The difference between them is the oil they brought.

records.source: μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς κραυγὴ γέγονεν· Ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος, ἐξέρχεσθε εἰς ἀπάντησιν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: At middle then of night a cry there was: Behold the bridegroom, go forth to meeting of him.
pieces: In the middle of the night a shout was heard: 'The bridegroom is here! Go out to meet him.'

L.6: And at midnight there was a cry, 'Look, the bridegroom! Go out to meet him.'

R.6: At midnight someone shouted, 'The bridegroom is here! Go out and meet him!'

decisions.choice: there was a cry: told vividly with a perfect tense
decisions.reason: The tense makes the moment vivid; it describes one shout at midnight.

decisions.choice: look (L); "is here" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: him, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The bridegroom is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no span, as in 9:15 and John 3:29, though the story points to the Son of Man's coming.

records.source: τότε ἠγέρθησαν πᾶσαι αἱ παρθένοι ἐκεῖναι καὶ ἐκόσμησαν τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν.
records.gloss: Then arose all the virgins those and trimmed the lamps of them.
pieces: Then all the young women woke up and got their lamps ready.

L.7: Then all those virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.

R.7: Then all the young women woke up and got their lamps ready to burn brightly.

decisions.choice: trimmed: put in order, by trimming the wick or adding oil
decisions.reason: The verb means to put in order. A lamp or torch was made to burn well again before the procession.

decisions.choice: got their lamps ready
decisions.reason: "Trimmed" is a technical word few readers know. Balanced and Readable say what the women did.

records.source: αἱ δὲ μωραὶ ταῖς φρονίμοις εἶπαν· Δότε ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ ἐλαίου ὑμῶν, ὅτι αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῶν σβέννυνται.
records.gloss: The and foolish to the wise said: Give us of the oil of you, for the lamps of us are going out.
pieces: The foolish ones said to the wise, 'Share some of your oil with us; our lamps are going out.'

L.8: And the foolish said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.'

R.8: The foolish ones said to the wise ones, 'Please give us some of your oil. Our lamps are about to go out.'

decisions.choice: are going out: in the process of going out
decisions.reason: The present tense shows the flames dying, not already dead.

records.source: ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ αἱ φρόνιμοι λέγουσαι· Μήποτε οὐ μὴ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν· πορεύεσθε μᾶλλον πρὸς τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράσατε ἑαυταῖς.
records.gloss: Answered then the wise saying: Lest not not it suffice for us and you; go rather to those selling and buy for yourselves.
pieces: But the wise ones replied, 'We cannot; there would surely not be enough for both you and us. You had better go to the oil sellers and buy your own.'

L.9: But the wise answered, saying, '[No,] lest there not be enough for us and for you; go instead to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.'

R.9: The wise ones answered, 'No. If we give you some, there will not be enough for any of us. Go to the people who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.'

decisions.choice: lest there not be enough: a refusal with a strong reason
decisions.reason: The opening word expresses a fear, and the double negative makes it strong. The answer is no, because sharing would leave all ten without light.

decisions.choice: those who sell: oil sellers in the town
decisions.reason: The advice is practical, but at midnight it means being away when the bridegroom comes.

decisions.choice: [No,] (L); We cannot (B); No (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek implies the refusal before giving the reason; each level states it.

records.source: ἀπερχομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀγοράσαι ἦλθεν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ αἱ ἕτοιμοι εἰσῆλθον μετ’ αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ ἐκλείσθη ἡ θύρα.
records.gloss: While going away then they to buy came the bridegroom, and those ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and was shut the door.
pieces: While they were off buying it, the bridegroom arrived. The ones who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was closed.

L.10: And while they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.

R.10: So they went to buy oil. While they were gone, the bridegroom came. The young women who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast. Then someone shut the door.

decisions.choice: ready: prepared for the bridegroom's coming
decisions.reason: The word picks up 24:44, "you also must be ready". Readiness is the point of the parable.

decisions.choice: the door was shut: no one else could come in
alternatives: the door was closed for the night only
decisions.reason: The shut door means the time for entering is over, as the next verses show.

decisions.choice: someone shut the door
decisions.reason: Readable uses an active sentence; the Greek does not say who shut it.

records.source: ὕστερον δὲ ἔρχονται καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ παρθένοι λέγουσαι· Κύριε κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν·
records.gloss: Afterward then come also the other virgins saying: Lord lord, open to us;
pieces: Later the rest of the young women came as well. 'Lord, lord,' they cried, 'open the door for us!'

L.11: And afterward the other virgins also come, saying, 'Lord, lord, open to us.'

R.11: Later the other young women came back. They called out, 'Lord, lord, open the door and let us in!'

decisions.choice: Lord, lord: an echo of 7:21-22
decisions.reason: The double address is what a guest would say to the master of the feast, but it repeats the words of those who are turned away in 7:21-23. The story points to the Lord's coming.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: Lord, lord
decisions.reason: Keeping "Lord" at every level lets the reader hear the echo of 7:21-22. The second word is lowercase because the speaker is a figure in a parable.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς.
records.gloss: He but answering said: Truly I say to you, not I know you.
pieces: But he replied, 'Truly I tell you, I do not know you.'

L.12: But he answered and said, 'Truly I tell you, I do not know you.'

R.12: But he answered, 'I tell you the truth, I do not know you.'

decisions.choice: I do not know you: I do not own you as mine
alternatives: I do not recognize your faces
decisions.reason: As in 7:23, "I never knew you", the words disown them. They are not counted among the bridegroom's guests.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening keeps the settled wording.

records.source: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ὥραν.
records.gloss: Watch therefore, for not you know the day nor the hour.
pieces: Keep awake, then, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

L.13: Keep awake, therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

R.13: So stay awake and be ready! You do not know the day or the hour.

decisions.choice: keep awake: stay alert and ready
decisions.reason: All ten slept (25:5), so the command is not about sleep. It means to live ready for the Lord's coming, as in 24:42.

decisions.choice: the day nor the hour, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "in which the Son of Man is coming", making plain what 24:44 already says. The earliest manuscripts end with "the hour". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: stay awake and be ready
decisions.reason: Readable adds "be ready", following the meaning decision.

records.source: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος ἀποδημῶν ἐκάλεσεν τοὺς ἰδίους δούλους καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ μὲν ἔδωκεν πέντε τάλαντα ᾧ δὲ δύο ᾧ δὲ ἕν, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.
records.gloss: Just as for a man going on a journey called the own slaves and handed over to them the possessions of him, \v 15 and to one he gave five talents, to one two, to one one, to each according to the own ability, and went on a journey.
pieces: It is like a man about to travel abroad. He summoned his own servants and handed his property over to them.
He gave {{units:five bags of silver|five talents}} to one, two to another and one to a third, according to what each could manage. Then he set off.

L.14: For [it is] just as a man going on a journey called his own slaves and handed over to them his possessions,
L.15: and to one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his own ability, and he went on his journey.

R.14: It will also be like a man who was going away on a trip. He called his servants and put them in charge of his money.
R.15: He gave {{units:five bags of silver|five talents}} to one servant, two to another, and one to another. (Each one was worth about twenty years' pay for a worker.) He gave each servant an amount that matched what he was able to handle. Then he left on his trip.

decisions.choice: for it is like: the comparison continues from 25:1, the kingdom at the Son of Man's coming
decisions.reason: The sentence has no stated subject. "For" ties it to the call to watch in 25:13.

decisions.choice: talent: a large weight of silver, about twenty years' wages for a laborer
decisions.reason: A talent was about 6,000 denarii, and a denarius was a day's pay for a laborer (20:2). Even one talent was a fortune. The later use of the word for a natural ability comes from this parable.

decisions.choice: slaves: entrusted with the master's business
decisions.reason: Slaves in a wealthy household could manage money and trade for their master. The word is the one for a slave, as in 24:45-51.

decisions.choice: {{units:five bags of silver|five talents}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the sum by default, with the original unit as the alternative. Literal keeps the talent.

decisions.choice: his, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no span, as with the bridegroom in 25:6.

decisions.choice: Each one was worth about twenty years' pay for a worker.
decisions.reason: Readable says how large the sums were, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.heading: Servants entrusted with their master's money

records.source: εὐθέως πορευθεὶς ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν ἠργάσατο ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα πέντε·
records.gloss: Immediately \v 16 having gone the one the five talents having received traded with them and gained other five;
pieces: At once
the servant with the {{units:five bags|five talents}} went and did business with them and made five more.

L.16: the one who had received the five talents went and traded with them and gained five more;

R.16: the servant with the {{units:five bags of silver|five talents}} went and used the money to do business. He earned five more.

decisions.choice: immediately: with the slave's going to work, as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: with the master's going away: "and he went away at once"
decisions.reason: The word stands between the two sentences. Taken with what follows, it shows the first slave's eagerness. Other editions end verse 15 with it.

decisions.choice: traded: did business with the money
decisions.reason: The verb means to work, here to put money to work in trade.

records.source: ὡσαύτως ὁ τὰ δύο ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα δύο·
records.gloss: Likewise the one the two gained other two;
pieces: In the same way the one with two made two more.

L.17: likewise the one [with] the two gained two more.

R.17: The servant with {{units:two bags|two talents}} did the same and earned two more.

decisions.choice: likewise: by trading in the same way
decisions.reason: The second slave did what the first did, with the same result for the sum entrusted.

records.source: ὁ δὲ τὸ ἓν λαβὼν ἀπελθὼν ὤρυξεν γῆν καὶ ἔκρυψεν τὸ ἀργύριον τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: The one but the one having received having gone away dug ground and hid the money of the master of him.
pieces: The servant who had received only one, however, went away and buried his master's money in a hole in the ground.

L.18: But the one who had received the one went away and dug in [the] ground and hid his master's money.

R.18: But the servant with {{units:one bag|one talent}} went and dug a hole in the ground. He hid his master's money there.

decisions.choice: hiding money in the ground: a common way to keep it safe
decisions.reason: Burying was a usual way to keep valuables from thieves (13:44). The slave keeps the money safe but does nothing with it.

decisions.choice: money: literally silver
decisions.reason: The word means silver and so money.

records.source: μετὰ δὲ πολὺν χρόνον ἔρχεται ὁ κύριος τῶν δούλων ἐκείνων καὶ συναίρει λόγον μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν προσήνεγκεν ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα λέγων· Κύριε, πέντε τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
records.gloss: After then much time comes the master of the slaves those and settles account with them. \v 20 And having come the one the five talents having received brought other five talents saying: Master, five talents to me you handed over; look, other five talents I gained.
pieces: A long time afterward the master of those servants returned and went over the accounts with them.

The one who had received {{units:five bags of silver|five talents}} came and brought five more. 'Master,' he said, 'you put {{units:five bags of silver|five talents}} in my care. See, I have made five more.'

L.19: And after a long time the master of those slaves comes and settles accounts with them.
L.20: And the one who had received the five talents came and brought five more talents, saying, 'Master, you handed over five talents to me; look, I have gained five more talents.'

R.19: After a long time the master came back. He asked his servants to show him what they had done with his money.
R.20: The servant who had received {{units:five bags of silver|five talents}} came and brought five more. He said, 'Master, you gave me {{units:five bags|five talents}}. Look, I have earned five more.'

decisions.choice: after a long time: the master's return is delayed
decisions.reason: Like the bridegroom's delay (25:5), the long time points to a wait before the Son of Man comes.

decisions.choice: settles accounts: makes them report on what they did with his money
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from business and is used again in 18:23.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration for both verbs.

decisions.choice: look (L, R); see (B)
decisions.reason: The slave points to the money he has brought, so the word is kept in his speech.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
records.gloss: Said to him the master of him: Well, slave good and faithful, over a few you were faithful, over many you I will set; enter into the joy of the master of you.
pieces: His master answered, 'Well done! You are a good and faithful servant. You proved faithful in small matters; I will put you in charge of great ones. Come in and share the joy of your master.'

L.21: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful slave; you were faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things; enter into the joy of your master.'

R.21: His master said, 'Well done! You are a good servant, and you can be trusted. You were faithful with a small amount, so I will put you in charge of much more. Come and share your master's joy!'

decisions.choice: faithful: trustworthy with what was entrusted
decisions.reason: The word describes a slave who can be relied on. The same pair, faithful and wise, describes the good slave in 24:45.

decisions.choice: a few things: small in comparison with what comes next
decisions.reason: Five talents was a fortune, yet it is "a few things" beside what the master will now give.

decisions.choice: the joy of your master: the master's own joy and celebration, which the slave now shares
decisions.reason: The slave is invited to share his master's gladness, and perhaps his feast. The picture points to the joy of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: you can be trusted
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the first "faithful" and keeps "faithful" in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὰ δύο τάλαντα εἶπεν· Κύριε, δύο τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα δύο τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
records.gloss: Having come and also the one the two talents said: Master, two talents to me you handed over; look, other two talents I gained.
pieces: The one with the {{units:two bags of silver|two talents}} came too. 'Master,' he said, 'you put {{units:two bags of silver|two talents}} in my care. See, I have made two more.'

L.22: And the one with the two talents also came and said, 'Master, you handed over two talents to me; look, I have gained two more talents.'

R.22: The servant with the {{units:two bags of silver|two talents}} came too. He said, 'Master, you gave me {{units:two bags|two talents}}. Look, I have earned two more.'

decisions.choice: also: the second slave's report matches the first
decisions.reason: His words repeat the first slave's in the same order. The amount differs, the faithfulness is the same.

decisions.choice: look (L, R); see (B)
decisions.reason: As in 25:20, the word is kept in the slave's speech.

records.source: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
records.gloss: Said to him the master of him: Well, slave good and faithful, over a few you were faithful, over many you I will set; enter into the joy of the master of you.
pieces: His master answered, 'Well done! You are a good and faithful servant. You proved faithful in small matters; I will put you in charge of great ones. Come in and share the joy of your master.'

L.23: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful slave; you were faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things; enter into the joy of your master.'

R.23: His master said, 'Well done! You are a good servant, and you can be trusted. You were faithful with a small amount, so I will put you in charge of much more. Come and share your master's joy!'

decisions.choice: the same words as 25:21
decisions.reason: The master answers the slave with two talents exactly as he answered the one with five. He rewards faithfulness, not the size of the gain.

decisions.choice: the joy of your master: as in 25:21
decisions.reason: The slave is invited to share his master's gladness.

decisions.choice: the wording of 25:21 at each level
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats 25:21 word for word, so each level repeats it too.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὸ ἓν τάλαντον εἰληφὼς εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἔγνων σε ὅτι σκληρὸς εἶ ἄνθρωπος, θερίζων ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρας καὶ συνάγων ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισας·
records.gloss: Having come then also the one the one talent having received said: Master, I knew you that hard you are a man, reaping where not you sowed and gathering from where not you scattered;
pieces: Then the one who had received the {{units:one bag of silver|one talent}} came. 'Master,' he said, 'I knew how hard a man you are. You reap fields you never sowed and gather grain where you scattered no seed.

L.24: And the one who had received the one talent also came and said, 'Master, I knew you, that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter;

R.24: Then the servant who had received {{units:one bag of silver|one talent}} came. He said, 'Master, I knew that you are a harsh man who demands a lot. You harvest crops from fields you did not plant. You gather grain where you did not scatter any seed.

decisions.choice: hard: harsh and demanding
decisions.reason: The slave blames the master's character for his own fear. The word means harsh or severe.

decisions.choice: reaping where he did not sow: taking profit from others' work
decisions.reason: The slave pictures the master as one who takes a harvest he did not plant. "Scatter" may mean sowing seed or winnowing grain; either way he gains from what he did not do.

decisions.choice: grain, seed
alternatives: gathering where you did not scatter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is gathered and scattered so the farming picture is clear.

records.source: καὶ φοβηθεὶς ἀπελθὼν ἔκρυψα τὸ τάλαντόν σου ἐν τῇ γῇ· ἴδε ἔχεις τὸ σόν.
records.gloss: And having been afraid having gone away I hid the talent of you in the ground; look, you have the yours.
pieces: I was afraid, so I went off and buried your {{units:bag of silver|talent}} in the ground. Here it is; you have what is yours.'

L.25: and being afraid, I went away and hid your talent in the ground; look, you have what is yours.'

R.25: I was afraid, so I went and hid your {{units:bag of silver|talent}} in the ground. Here is your money back.'

decisions.choice: being afraid: fear is the reason he gives
decisions.reason: The slave says fear of the master kept him from using the money.

decisions.choice: you have what is yours: he gives back exactly what he was given
decisions.reason: He returns the talent untouched and thinks that is enough.

decisions.choice: Here it is (B); Here is (R)
decisions.reason: The slave holds out the money, and Balanced and Readable say so in the way people hand something over.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πονηρὲ δοῦλε καὶ ὀκνηρέ, ᾔδεις ὅτι θερίζω ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρα καὶ συνάγω ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισα;
records.gloss: Answering now the master of him said to him: Wicked slave and lazy, you knew that I reap where not I sowed and gather from where not I scattered?
pieces: His master replied, 'You wicked, lazy servant! So you knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter?

L.26: But his master answered and said to him, 'Wicked and lazy slave! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter?

R.26: His master answered, 'You are an evil and lazy servant! You say you knew that I harvest where I did not plant and gather where I did not scatter seed.

decisions.choice: you knew ...: the master repeats the slave's words to judge him by them
alternatives: the master admits he is harsh
decisions.reason: The master does not agree that he is hard. He takes the slave at his word: if he believed it, he should have acted on it (25:27). The sentence may be read as a question or as a statement.

decisions.choice: wicked and lazy: the slave's fault is unwillingness, not inability
decisions.reason: He was given one talent according to his ability (25:15), and did nothing with it.

decisions.choice: You say you knew ... (a statement)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the master's point with a statement.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἔδει σε οὖν βαλεῖν τὰ ἀργύριά μου τοῖς τραπεζίταις, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐγὼ ἐκομισάμην ἂν τὸ ἐμὸν σὺν τόκῳ.
records.gloss: It behooved you therefore to put the money of me to the bankers, and having come I would have received the my own with interest.
pieces: In that case you should have handed my money to the bankers. On my return I would at least have got back what is mine, with interest.

L.27: Then you ought to have put my money with the bankers, and when I came I would have received what is mine with interest.

R.27: Then you should have put my money in the bank. When I came back, I would at least have gotten it back with some interest.

decisions.choice: bankers: money changers and lenders who paid interest on deposits
decisions.reason: The word comes from the tables at which money changers worked (21:12). They took deposits and lent money at interest.

decisions.choice: with interest: the least he could have done
decisions.reason: Putting money with the bankers needed no effort or risk. The slave did not do even that.

decisions.choice: at least
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that this was the smallest return possible, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: in the bank
decisions.reason: Readable uses the modern equivalent of a banker's deposit.

records.source: ἄρατε οὖν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ τάλαντον καὶ δότε τῷ ἔχοντι τὰ δέκα τάλαντα·
records.gloss: Take therefore from him the talent and give to the one having the ten talents;
pieces: So take the {{units:bag of silver|talent}} away from him and give it to the servant who has {{units:ten bags|ten talents}}.

L.28: So take the talent from him and give [it] to the one who has the ten talents.

R.28: Take the {{units:bag of silver|talent}} away from him. Give it to the servant who has {{units:ten bags|ten talents}}.

decisions.choice: take, give: commands to those standing by
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural. The master speaks to others in the household.

decisions.choice: the ten talents: the first slave's five and the five he gained
decisions.reason: The first slave now holds ten talents.

records.source: τῷ γὰρ ἔχοντι παντὶ δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται· τοῦ δὲ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: To the for having everyone will be given and he will have abundance; of the but not having even what he has will be taken away from him.
pieces: For everyone who has will be given more, and {{gender:they|he}} will have more than enough. But anyone who has nothing will lose even what {{gender:they have|he has}}.

L.29: For to everyone who has, [more] will be given, and {{gender:they|he}} will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what {{gender:they have|he has}} will be taken away from {{gender:them|him}}.

R.29: People who have something will be given more, and they will have more than they need. But people who have nothing will lose even the little they have.

decisions.choice: to everyone who has, more will be given: the saying of 13:12
decisions.reason: Jesus used the same saying of those who receive his teaching (13:12). Those who use what God gives receive more; those who neglect it lose even that.

decisions.choice: will be given, will be taken: God's action in the judgment
decisions.reason: The passives point to the judgment the parable describes.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: The saying applies to anyone, so the inclusive form is the default. Readable uses the plural.

decisions.choice: the little they have
decisions.reason: Readable says that what is taken is small, as the one talent was beside ten.

records.source: καὶ τὸν ἀχρεῖον δοῦλον ἐκβάλετε εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
records.gloss: And the worthless slave cast out into the darkness the outer; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
pieces: Throw this useless servant out into the darkness outside, where people will weep and grind their teeth.'

L.30: And throw the worthless slave into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'

R.30: Throw this useless servant outside into the dark. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'

decisions.choice: the outer darkness, weeping and gnashing of teeth: exclusion and anguish
alternatives: a literal place described in detail
decisions.reason: As in 8:12, the darkness outside the lighted feast pictures being shut out of the kingdom, and grinding the teeth shows anguish and rage. The wording follows 8:12 at each level.

decisions.choice: worthless: of no use to his master
decisions.reason: The word means unprofitable. The slave brought his master nothing.

decisions.choice: there will be weeping: the parable's words point beyond the story
alternatives: only the master's words in the story
decisions.reason: The phrase is Jesus's own way of speaking of the final judgment (13:42; 24:51), so the master's sentence turns into a warning to the hearers.

decisions.choice: useless
decisions.reason: "Useless" says plainly what the slave was to his master.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι μετ’ αὐτοῦ, τότε καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: When then comes the Son of the Man in the glory of him and all the angels with him, then he will sit on throne of glory of him;
pieces: The Son of Man will come in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and all the angels with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat on the throne of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

L.31: And when the Son of Man comes in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and all the angels with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sit on [the] throne of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory;

R.31: The Son of Man will come in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and all the angels will come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sit on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious throne.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming in glory: Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: In Daniel one like a son of man comes before God and is given glory and a kingdom over all peoples. Jesus applies the picture to himself (24:30; 26:64).

decisions.choice: glory: the splendor and majesty of God's king
decisions.reason: The throne of his glory is the throne from which he rules and judges, as in 19:28.

decisions.choice: he will sit on the throne: the Son of Man is the judge
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as the one who judges all people (7:22-23; 16:27).

decisions.choice: his, him, he with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Unlike the figures in the parables before it, the Son of Man here is Jesus himself, so his pronouns take the usual span.

decisions.choice: glorious throne
decisions.reason: Readable uses the adjective, which keeps the key term.

records.heading: The Son of Man judges the nations

records.source: καὶ συναχθήσονται ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἀφορίσει αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων, ὥσπερ ὁ ποιμὴν ἀφορίζει τὰ πρόβατα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρίφων, καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων.
records.gloss: And will be gathered before him all the nations, and he will separate them from one another, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats, \v 33 and he will set the sheep on right of him, the but goats on left.
pieces: Every nation will be brought together before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will divide the people into two groups, the way a shepherd sorts the sheep from the goats.
He will stand the sheep at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand and the goats at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.

L.32: And all the nations will be gathered before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will separate them from one another, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,
L.33: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set the sheep on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, but the goats on [the] left.

R.32: People from every nation will be gathered in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will separate them into two groups, like a shepherd who separates the sheep from the goats.
R.33: He will put the sheep on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right side and the goats on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.

decisions.choice: all the nations: all people of every nation
decisions.reason: "Them" in the next clause is masculine, so the people of the nations are meant, judged one by one. Whether Israel is included is debated; the scene seems to include all humanity.

decisions.choice: the shepherd separates sheep from goats: a daily task
alternatives: a picture of choosing better animals
decisions.reason: Sheep and goats grazed together in one flock and were separated, often at evening. The picture is of a simple sorting, not of the worth of the animals.

decisions.choice: right and left: the place of honor and its opposite
decisions.reason: To sit or stand at a ruler's right hand was the place of favor (Psalm 110:1).

decisions.choice: the people; into two groups
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is separated and how, following the meaning decision.

records.source: τότε ἐρεῖ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
records.gloss: Then will say the King to those on right of him: Come, the blessed of the Father of me, inherit the having been prepared for you kingdom from foundation of world.
pieces: Then the King will say to those at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, 'Come, you whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father has blessed. The kingdom has been ready for you since the world was founded; now it is yours to inherit.

L.34: Then the King will say to those on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, 'Come, you blessed of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from [the] foundation of [the] world.

R.34: Then the King will say to the people on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right, 'Come, you people {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father has blessed! Receive the kingdom as your own. It has been ready and waiting for you since the world was made.

decisions.choice: the King: the Son of Man himself
decisions.reason: The King speaks of "my Father", so he is the Son of Man of 25:31, now named as king (compare 2:2; 27:11).

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as a gift that belongs to God's children
decisions.reason: An inheritance is not earned. The kingdom was prepared for them long before they acted.

decisions.choice: from the foundation of the world: from the beginning of creation
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 13:35. God's plan for his people was made before history began.

decisions.choice: King, with a capital
decisions.reason: The title belongs to the Son of Man himself, so it is capitalized, and his pronouns take the usual span.

decisions.choice: Receive the kingdom as your own
decisions.reason: Readable says what inheriting means without the legal word.

records.source: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ περιεβάλετέ με, ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με, ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθατε πρός με.
records.gloss: I hungered for and you gave me to eat, I thirsted and you gave drink me, a stranger I was and you took in me, \v 36 naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, in prison I was and you came to me.
pieces: For when I was hungry, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} food; when I was thirsty, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a drink; when I was a stranger, you took {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into your home;
when I had no clothes, you dressed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; when I was sick, you looked after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; when I was in prison, you came to see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

L.35: For I was hungry and you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [something] to eat, I was thirsty and you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} drink, I was a stranger and you took {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in,
L.36: naked and you clothed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I was sick and you visited {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I was in prison and you came to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

R.35: When I was hungry, you fed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When I was thirsty, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water. When I was a stranger, you let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stay with you.
R.36: When I had no clothes, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} clothes to wear. When I was sick, you took care of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When I was in prison, you came to visit {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: a stranger: a traveler or foreigner far from home who needs a place to stay
decisions.reason: Hospitality to strangers was a duty the law commanded (Leviticus 19:34). To take in means to receive into one's home.

decisions.choice: naked: without enough clothing
decisions.reason: The word is used of someone poorly clothed as well as of someone with no clothes.

decisions.choice: visited: came to help and care for
decisions.reason: The verb means to look after someone in need.

decisions.choice: I was hungry: the King names himself in those who were in need
decisions.reason: The righteous are surprised by this (25:37-39), and the King explains it in 25:40.

decisions.choice: me with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The King is the Son of Man speaking of himself, so "me" takes the usual span.

records.source: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν, ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν;
records.gloss: Then will answer him the righteous saying: Lord, when you did we see hungering and fed, or thirsting and gave drink?
pieces: Then the righteous will reply, 'Lord, when was it that we saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry and fed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, or thirsty and gave {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a drink?

L.37: Then the righteous will answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, 'Lord, when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry and feed [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}], or thirsty and give [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] drink?

R.37: Then the righteous people will answer, 'Lord, when did we ever see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry and give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} food? When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thirsty and give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} something to drink?

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who do what is right in God's eyes
decisions.reason: The word describes those on the King's right. Their surprise shows they did not act to earn a reward.

decisions.choice: when did we see you: a real question of surprise
decisions.reason: They did not know that they were serving the King.

decisions.choice: him, you with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: They speak to the King, the Son of Man, so "you" takes the usual span.

records.source: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν, ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν;
records.gloss: When now you did we see a stranger and took in, or naked and clothed?
pieces: When was it that we saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a stranger and welcomed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in, or without clothes and dressed {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?

L.38: And when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a stranger and take [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] in, or naked and clothe [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}]?

R.38: When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} as a stranger and invite {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} into our homes? When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} without clothes and give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} clothes to wear?

decisions.choice: the questions follow the King's list in order
decisions.reason: The righteous repeat each need the King named in 25:35-36.

records.source: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ἀσθενοῦντα ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρός σε;
records.gloss: When now you did we see being sick or in prison and came to you?
pieces: When was it that we saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sick or in prison and came to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'

L.39: And when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sick or in prison and come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'

R.39: When did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sick or in prison and come to visit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'

decisions.choice: in prison: prisoners depended on visitors for food and care
decisions.reason: Prisons gave little food or care, so visits could mean survival.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ’ ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
records.gloss: And answering the King will say to them: Truly I say to you, to the extent that you did to one of these the brothers of me the least, to me you did.
pieces: The King will answer them, 'Truly I tell you, each time you did it for one of these {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, even the least of them, you did it for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

L.40: And the King will answer and say to them, 'Truly I tell you, as much as you did [it] to one of the least of these {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you did [it] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

R.40: And the King will answer, 'I tell you the truth, whenever you did these things for even the least important of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, you were doing them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: the least of these my brothers: Jesus's followers in need
alternatives: anyone in need, believer or not
decisions.reason: Jesus calls his disciples his brothers (12:49-50; 28:10) and promises that whoever helps one of these little ones will be rewarded (10:40-42). Others read the words of every needy person, since the King names himself in all who suffer. The passage does not settle it.

decisions.choice: brothers: men and women alike
decisions.reason: The word in the plural often means brothers and sisters together (12:50).

decisions.choice: you did it to me: what is done to them is done to the King himself
alternatives: only counted as if it were done to him
decisions.reason: Jesus identifies himself with his brothers, as in 10:40: "Whoever welcomes you welcomes me."

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The word includes women, so the inclusive form is the default and the traditional form is the alternative.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 25:12, the solemn opening keeps the settled wording.

records.source: τότε ἐρεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἐξ εὐωνύμων· Πορεύεσθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ οἱ κατηραμένοι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον τὸ ἡτοιμασμένον τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Then he will say also to those on left: Depart from me those having been cursed into the fire the eternal the having been prepared for the devil and the angels of him.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say to those at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left, 'Go away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who are under a curse, into the eternal fire that has been made ready for the devil and his angels.

L.41: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say also to those on [the] left, 'Depart from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

R.41: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say to the people on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left, 'Go away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you people who are under a curse! Go into the eternal fire. It was made ready for the devil and his angels.

decisions.choice: depart from me: as in 7:23
decisions.reason: The King uses the words of 7:23, which echo Psalm 6:8.

decisions.choice: cursed, and a fire prepared for the devil: not prepared for them
alternatives: cursed by the Father, a fire made for people
decisions.reason: The blessed are blessed "of my Father" and the kingdom was prepared for them (25:34). Here neither is said: the curse is not called the Father's, and the fire was prepared for the devil and his angels.

decisions.choice: eternal: belonging to the age to come, without end
decisions.reason: The same word describes both the punishment and the life in 25:46.

decisions.choice: Depart (L); Go away (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:23, Literal keeps "depart" and Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: he, me with deity_pronoun spans; his angels with none
alternatives: a span on the devil's angels
decisions.reason: The King's pronouns take the span. "His angels" are the devil's.

records.source: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με, ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με.
records.gloss: I hungered for and not you gave me to eat, I thirsted and not you gave drink me, \v 43 a stranger I was and not you took in me, naked and not you clothed me, sick and in prison and not you visited me.
pieces: For when I was hungry, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no food; when I was thirsty, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} nothing to drink;

when I was a stranger, you did not take {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into your home; when I had no clothes, you did not dress {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; when I was sick and in prison, you did not look after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

L.42: For I was hungry and you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [anything] to eat, I was thirsty and you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} drink,
L.43: I was a stranger and you did not take {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in, naked and you did not clothe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, sick and in prison and you did not visit {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

R.42: When I was hungry, you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} food. When I was thirsty, you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water.
R.43: When I was a stranger, you did not let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} stay with you. When I had no clothes, you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} clothes to wear. When I was sick and in prison, you did not come to take care of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: the list repeats 25:35-36 with each act left undone
decisions.reason: The judgment rests on what they failed to do. The last two needs are joined, shortening the list.

decisions.choice: the wording of 25:35-36, made negative
decisions.reason: Each level repeats its own wording of 25:35-36 so the two lists can be compared.

records.source: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι;
records.gloss: Then will answer also they saying: Lord, when you did we see hungering or thirsting or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and not did minister to you?
pieces: Then they too will reply, 'Lord, when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry or thirsty, a stranger or without clothes, sick or in prison, and not come to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help?'

L.44: Then they also will answer, saying, 'Lord, when did we see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'

R.44: Then these people will answer, 'Lord, when did we ever see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or without clothes, or sick, or in prison, and not help {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?'

decisions.choice: serve: meet the needs of
decisions.reason: The verb is used of all kinds of care, from serving food to providing for someone (27:55).

decisions.choice: when did we see you: they too are surprised
alternatives: an excuse that they would have helped
decisions.reason: Like the righteous, they did not know the King was in those in need.

decisions.choice: come to your help
decisions.reason: Balanced says what serving meant here; Literal keeps "serve".

records.source: τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ’ ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων, οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
records.gloss: Then he will answer them saying: Truly I say to you, to the extent that not you did to one of these the least, neither to me you did.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reply, 'Truly I tell you, each time you failed to do it for one of these, even the least of them, you failed to do it for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

L.45: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will answer them, saying, 'Truly I tell you, as much as you did not do [it] to one of the least of these, you did not do [it] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} either.'

R.45: Then the King will answer, 'I tell you the truth, when you did not do these things for even the least important of these, you did not do them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: one of the least of these: the same people as in 25:40
decisions.reason: "My brothers" is not repeated, but the phrase points back to 25:40.

decisions.choice: nor to me: neglecting them is neglecting the King
decisions.reason: The King is identified with them in neglect as in kindness.

decisions.choice: the King
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.source: καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
records.gloss: And will go away these into punishment eternal, the but righteous into life eternal.
pieces: These will depart to eternal punishment, and the righteous will go to eternal life."

L.46: And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life."

R.46: Then these people will go away to eternal punishment. But the righteous people will go to eternal life."

decisions.choice: eternal: belonging to the age to come, without end
decisions.reason: The same word describes the punishment and the life, setting them side by side (Daniel 12:2). Whether the punishment is conscious without end or a ruin that cannot be undone is not settled by this verse (compare 10:28).

decisions.choice: punishment: penalty given in judgment
decisions.reason: The word can mean correction, but here it is the judge's sentence.

decisions.choice: the end of Jesus's speech that began at 24:4
decisions.reason: The teaching on the Mount of Olives ends here; 26:1 returns to the story.
